verdict.line: You lose if you walk into Corrosive Charge and Purge poke before level 6 with no way to close the gap; you win once Path Maker and All Out let you force the fight on your terms.

brief.thesis: Urgot has no way to interrupt a charged, committed approach except E (Disdain), a 475-range dash with a 16/15.5/15/14.5/14s cooldown — everything else he has is poke, not peel. K'Sante has almost no reliable gap-closer until W (Path Maker) and R (All Out) come online, so the lane is a patience check pre-6 and a forced fight after it. The 47.4% win rate over 867 games reflects a lane that is close but structurally tilted toward whoever plays their power spikes correctly.

theirWindow.when: his E (Disdain) is up, you're poked low
theirWindow.what: Don't dash in a straight line at him. If you commit W (Path Maker) or walk up for Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks while Disdain is available, he can catch you mid-approach and fling you off path, wasting your engage and leaving you exposed to his 800-range Q (Corrosive Charge) and auto poke on the way back out.

yourWindow.what: This is your real window to close the gap. Walk up and land two Q (Ntofo Strikes) hits to trigger the shockwave pull, or commit W (Path Maker) for the stun — he has nothing left to stop the approach once Disdain is down.

start.why: Carries a 53.1% win rate over 177 games and its passive block/regen directly answers Urgot's auto-attack-reliant poke in a way Doran's Helm doesn't.

boots.why: 84.5% pick rate and the right call here specifically — Urgot's damage is almost entirely basic attacks and auto-triggered Echoing Flames, which Steelcaps directly reduces.

core.why: The slow on ability-hit is what finally lets you stick to a kiting ranged opponent after level 9 — this is the item that flips the lane.
Sustain and damage reduction against a lane built entirely around chip poke; matches the 47.4% win rate path over 57 games.
Stacking resistances scale your All Out healing and let you outlast his Purge windows in extended skirmishes.

urgot builds crit or lethality and his Purge burst starts threatening all-ins
his attack speed from Purge stacking is shredding you faster than expected

runes.keystoneWhy: The sustain from proc'ing Grasp on trades is what lets you survive his Q/auto poke before level 6, and the bonus health scales your All Out damage and healing later.

summoners.why: The highest-performing combo at 49.3% win rate and 77.5% pick rate — Urgot has no early dive pressure, so Teleport lets you reset after poke exchanges and return to contest plates instead of conceding the lane.

playing.title: Track his Disdain cooldown
playing.detail: Urgot's E (Disdain) is his only answer to your approach, on a 16-14s cooldown depending on rank. Whenever it's down, that's your signal to walk up and trade.

playing.title: Don't dash into a charged Disdain
playing.detail: Committing W (Path Maker) or walking a straight line at him while his E is up risks getting caught and thrown off-course mid-engage, wasting your stun window entirely.

playing.title: Farm Q stacks before all-in
playing.detail: Two hits of Q (Ntofo Strikes) trigger the shockwave pull, which is your only way to force him into range before Iceborn Gauntlet is online.

playing.title: Use R to invert his zoning
playing.detail: R (All Out) knocks him back through any wall in his path, then you dash after him transformed — this turns his own poke range against him the instant it's up at level 6.

playing.title: Play passive pre-6
playing.detail: Respect his 800-range Q (Corrosive Charge) and 490-range W (Purge) before level 6 — you have no reliable way to close that gap yet, so don't force trades.

playing.title: Save E for the slow, not just the gap-close
playing.detail: Footwork's shield is most valuable absorbing Corrosive Charge's hit, since getting slowed by it otherwise chains you into further poke.

playing.title: Respect his execute past level 6
playing.detail: R (Fear Beyond Death) threatens to execute you below a health threshold at 2500 range — back off CS rather than greed once you're low, especially after he hits 6.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoner spells, and all win-rate figures are measured from live games on the current patch (16.19.1) via OP.GG; the cooldowns, ranges, and tactical reasoning about when and how to use them are our own analysis layered on top.
